disposition_mapping.rationale: Extraction of locked-period actuals is mechanical data retrieval with no judgment content and already runs off the same period-lock trigger as comparative loading in practice. It is merged with VAR-02 into a single orchestrated ingestion step, but the locked-period gate remains an explicit, checkable input (per VAR-R-01, KB-03) rather than an implicit assumption, and the analyst retains an active, standing exception-review role rather than losing accountability to a silent pipeline.

Loading the approved budget version and latest forecast is equally mechanical and co-located with actuals extraction in one data-refresh job. The merge removes duplicate tooling/reconciliation overhead without removing the function: both required inputs remain explicit, separately labelled fields inside the merged step (per VAR-R-02), with version mismatches caught by the exception-review role rather than silently dropped.

The price/volume/mix decomposition becomes an engine-executed, versioned calculation rather than manual analyst arithmetic, since the judgment content is front-loaded into confirming the policy and FX parameters, not in performing the arithmetic itself. The analyst's role shifts to a documented pre-run sign-off on policy-version and FX-table-version currency, with a halt-on-mismatch safeguard. This satisfies VAR-R-05 and VAR-R-06 more robustly than ambient manual re-entry, and KB-08's requirement that FX effects stay separately visible is enforced by making the isolated FX variance a named output field rather than an internal computation detail.

Materiality screening remains a distinct, analyst-owned judgment step rather than being absorbed into the computation engine as a silent filter. Council consensus (five of seven members, with the sixth conceding this point in round 2) held that a pure percentage/absolute cutoff systematically misses qualitatively material items, and that the selecting actor must be a named human distinct from the reviewer for VAR-R-04 to mean anything beyond a nominal separation. Automation is used to generate the candidate flag list, but the inclusion/exclusion decision, with a bidirectional, documented override log, stays with the analyst. This preserves VAR-R-08 as a real, inspectable step rather than a function nested invisibly inside a larger automated span.

The function and actor (budget holders) are unchanged: commentary must remain genuine, human-authored narrative from the accountable business owner, not an AI-drafted text merely confirmed or overridden. The council firmly rejected AI pre-drafting (every member but one objected, and that member conceded in round 2) because a plausible pre-populated narrative converts a substantive accountability act into a rubber stamp under deadline pressure. What is restructured is purely the surrounding logistics: automated request generation, SLA tracking, asynchronous/offline-friendly collection, and escalation within the budget holder's own management line when a response lapses.

Consolidation of variances and commentary into a draft is templated and auto-assembled, since mechanical assembly of already-computed data and already-collected commentary carries no independent judgment content. The function is preserved through a mandatory analyst completeness check (no orphaned variances without commentary, no sign/driver mismatches) and strict provenance tagging distinguishing verbatim budget-holder text from system-assembled data, so the accountability chain from TS-04 is never silently broken by automated drafting.

Review and challenge survives unchanged in substance and is explicitly required to (VAR-R-07). It is strengthened, not weakened, by upstream automation: the manager now has direct access to the materiality override log and the policy/FX version stamps, not only a polished narrative, so challenge extends to the selection and computation basis rather than becoming ceremonial. The actor remains distinct from the TS-03 selector, satisfying VAR-R-04.

Presentation to management is retained as a distinct FP&A-manager accountability moment separate from review, per the majority view (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy) that standing behind numbers in front of an executive audience is a different accountability act than having challenged them in back-office review, and that collapsing the two removes the last point where a human can pull a report back before executive distribution. What is restructured is the distribution mechanics: automated, gated publication (firing only after TS-06 sign-off) with a logged send-record, a sign-off marker confirming the distributed version matches the reviewed version, and offline-consumable output formats alongside any dashboard so recipients without persistent connectivity are not excluded.

steps.actor: FP&A analyst (data steward) with automated ingestion job
steps.description: An automated, period-lock-triggered job pulls locked-period actuals and loads the approved budget version and latest forecast in a single orchestrated pass, producing a reconciled actuals-and-comparatives dataset. The job halts and raises an exception if the period is not locked, if a comparative version is missing, stale, or unapproved, or if a reconciliation-to-control-totals check fails. The FP&A analyst, acting as data steward, owns the exception log and resolves flagged mismatches (late-posting subledgers, un-baselined 'latest' forecasts) as a standing review each cycle, not only when an exception fires. The locked-period gate and the approved/latest version labels remain explicit, checkable fields, never implicit assumptions behind 'the extract already ran'.
steps.name: Automated extraction and load with analyst exception review

steps.actor: FP&A analyst (policy/FX configuration sign-off) with computation engine
steps.description: A rules-based computation engine applies the versioned price/volume/mix decomposition methodology to the reconciled dataset, consuming the accounting policies applied to actuals and the constant-currency exchange rates as explicit, versioned parameters. Before each run, the FP&A analyst signs off that the policy-version ID and FX-table-version ID in force match this period's approved values; the engine halts and routes to the analyst on any version mismatch or missing parameter rather than defaulting silently. The isolated FX effect is written to the output as a separately labeled field, never netted into price, volume or mix. Any divergence in accounting-policy basis between actuals and comparatives is surfaced as a flagged difference, not absorbed into a variance figure.
steps.name: Automated variance computation with policy/FX configuration sign-off
outputs: Variance dataset with isolated FX variance field
Policy-version ID and FX-table-version ID stamp

steps.description: An automated flagging pass applies the percentage and absolute materiality thresholds to the variance dataset to produce a candidate list, but the FP&A analyst retains ownership of the selection decision: the analyst reviews the flag list, may add sub-threshold items for documented qualitative reasons (first-occurrence control breaks, new-product-line items, recurring small misses), and may flag above-threshold items as noise for manager awareness without silently excluding them. Every inclusion and exclusion carries a logged rationale and the threshold value applied. This actor is organisationally and functionally distinct from the reviewer in TS-06.
inputs: Variance dataset with isolated FX variance field
steps.name: Materiality-based selection with analyst judgment and bidirectional override log

steps.actor: Budget holders (commentary authors); orchestration agent (logistics only)
steps.description: An orchestration layer auto-generates explanation requests from the selected variances, routes them to the identified accountable budget holder, and tracks response via asynchronous, store-and-forward mechanisms suitable for low-bandwidth or offline settings (structured templates returned by email or form, not dependent on live tooling). SLA deadlines are tracked and, where a response lapses, escalation runs within the budget holder's own management line (not to FP&A) so accountability for an unresponsive business owner stays inside the business. The commentary content itself is never system-drafted or pre-populated for the budget holder to merely confirm: it must originate as the accountable owner's own narrative.
steps.name: Commentary orchestration and collection

steps.description: A drafting agent auto-assembles the variance dataset and collected commentary into the report template. Every piece of text in the draft is provenance-tagged as either verbatim budget-holder commentary or system-assembled variance data, so no commentary is silently rewritten or summarised. The FP&A analyst performs a completeness check before the draft proceeds — confirming no selected variance is missing commentary, that commentary direction matches the variance's actual sign/driver, and that provenance tags are intact — and is the accountable owner of the draft that passes to review.
steps.name: Consolidation and draft report with provenance-tagged commentary and analyst completeness check

steps.description: The FP&A manager reviews and challenges the draft report, with direct access to the materiality override log from TS-03 and the policy-version/FX-table-version stamp from TS-02, not only the polished narrative, so that challenge extends to the underlying selection and computation basis and not merely prose quality. This actor is distinct from the analyst who performed selection in TS-03, preserving actor separation.
inputs: Policy-version ID and FX-table-version ID stamp
steps.name: Review and challenge

steps.description: The FP&A manager presents the reviewed report to management and remains the accountable actor for that presentation, as a distinct accountability moment from review. Mechanical distribution (publication/send) is automated and gated so it cannot fire against a report that has not cleared TS-06, with a logged send-record of recipients, timestamp and version. A sign-off marker confirms the distributed artifact matches the reviewed version exactly, closing any gap between review and distribution. Outputs are produced in lightweight, offline-consumable formats (PDF/spreadsheet) alongside any dashboard view, so recipients without persistent high-bandwidth access are not excluded.
steps.name: Present and distribute to management
